rai:dataCollection: The reservoir is assembled from public SRSD, LLM-SRBench, SRBench 1.0, SRBench2025, and classical symbolic-regression formula families. Upstream splits are preserved when available; formula-backed tasks without complete splits are materialized under the source-specific deterministic split policy described in the paper.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each task is normalized to a shared directory contract with train.csv, valid.csv, id_test.csv, optional ood_test.csv, metadata.yaml, and formula.py. Validation checks split presence, non-LFS content, consistent CSV headers, numeric columns, target and feature agreement, finite values, declared row counts, and formula replay. OOD data are generated only when a reliable formula and feature domain are available. Semantic duplicate detection and source-aware constraints are then applied before Core-50 selection.
rai:dataLimitations: Core-50 is a compact subset selected from a fixed 664-task ground-truth reservoir; conclusions may change for task families absent from that reservoir.

The benchmark evaluates black-box tabular symbolic regression with known ground-truth formulas and controlled splits. It is not validated as a universal measure of open-ended scientific discovery, causal identification, or performance on raw experimental data.
OOD coverage is source dependent. Tasks without a defensible OOD construction are excluded from OOD-dependent analyses rather than assigned fabricated OOD data.
Leaderboard results are conditional on the disclosed one-hour wall-clock protocol and should not be generalized to different compute, hardware, implementation, or tuning budgets.
rai:dataBiases: The reservoir inherits source-selection bias toward established symbolic-regression families, physics-style equations, and formula-backed tabular tasks.
Formula families, operator sets, feature dimensionalities, sample sizes, and OOD availability are unevenly represented; aggregate scores can therefore obscure family-specific behavior.
Core-50 selection is conditioned on the algorithms and objectives used during benchmark construction, so future algorithmic paradigms may motivate a versioned benchmark update.
rai:dataUseCases: Validated use: reproducible comparison of symbolic-regression algorithms under the released splits, failure semantics, one-hour budget, and fixed six-axis scoring protocol.
Validated use: auditing ID numerical quality, OOD generalization, symbolic fidelity, anytime efficiency, stability, and noisy-training robustness with the accompanying manifests and result schema.
Validated use: regression-testing new algorithm integrations without changing previously reported absolute scores.
Not validated for: ranking general scientific-discovery systems, making claims about causal discovery, or estimating performance on unmodeled real-world experimental noise.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential benefit: a standardized, auditable benchmark can reduce selective reporting and make symbolic-regression comparisons easier to reproduce. Potential risk: users may over-interpret small score differences, treat formula recovery as equivalent to scientific validity, or generalize controlled benchmark results to real scientific settings. Mitigation: the release preserves source-family labels, task-level artifacts, failure states, formulas, checksums, and multi-axis metrics so aggregate claims can be audited and qualified.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No human-subject, demographic, personally identifiable, or sensitive personal information is included.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenance: During review, the anonymized dataset page should remain accessible. After acceptance, anonymous review links should be replaced by a public archival release. Dataset and metadata changes should use versioned manifests and retained SHA256 checksums; benchmark-membership changes should be released as a new version rather than silently replacing Core-50.
